source_snapshot.procedure: Preserved 16-step workflow: install OS; remove AC for 30 seconds; power up; log into ILO; enter Advanced License; wait for Power Meter; record Maximum Available/Peak/Minimum; disable capping and stress 15 minutes; record again; capture Present Power; enable capping; set cap to Present Power; refresh 20-minute graph; record Average/Maximum excursions; then decrease cap about 5 W per iteration until an MSAC value described as obtained in a previous step. Afterward collect results/photos and inspect logs.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. System is capping the power utilization.
2. Average Power should be below Power Cap; Maximum Power may cross above it.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: Enable capping through BMC UI, use a user-selected cap, and inspect IPMI/Redfish power.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: Return PowerLimit and sensor values for user graph judgment.

original_test_intent: Validate system power-capping behavior under stress across progressively lower cap values, including Average/Maximum graph behavior down to MSAC.
original_method: Preserve all preparation, license, graph and iterative-decrement steps but do not run until the owner defines MSAC, a safe floor and stop rule, exact platform/tool applicability, sampling acceptance and complete restoration.
manual_activity: Engineer must define MSAC and safe sweep bounds, determine whether ILO/licensing applies to this Project, authorize OS/AC/workload disruption, and approve each observation/abort/restoration checkpoint.
required_inputs: Approved OS image and AC window
Watchdog, abort, final-state and recovery runbook
safety_requirements: No OS install, AC removal, license entry, cap write or stress in current form.
Never expose license or BMC credentials.
Do not decrement below an approved safe floor.
No log clearing or automatic retry.
Capture and restore all original cap/power/workload state.
agent_execution_scope: Static phase and evidence design only while blocked.
After correction, execute only an explicitly approved phase with one-attempt interlocks.
Perform bounded cap steps with stop conditions and synchronized graph/telemetry capture.
Restore state and return evidence without verdict.
engineer_actions: Define MSAC and the authoritative sweep algorithm.
Approve platform, license, disruption, workload and safety boundaries.
Own execution authorization, anomaly disposition and verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not executable or coverage-equivalent: it only gestures at enable/read operations and omits the preserved OS/AC setup, disabled baseline, 15-minute stress, 20-minute graph, iterative 5 W sweep, MSAC and recovery.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No command until owner correction; then use an approved vendor interface with typed cap writes/readbacks and an independently monitored bounded state machine.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: 30-second unplug, >=5-minute warm-up, 15-minute stress, 20-minute graph, approximately 5 W steps, MSAC wording and 20/60-minute metadata are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Split setup, baseline, cap step, stress observation, MSAC search and restoration into approved interlocked phases after semantics are fixed.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Undetermined until ILO/license versus Project BMC applicability is confirmed.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Pin firmware, license, UI/API, OS and stress package.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor cap/MSAC specification plus Project power/thermal/performance plan.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds explicit bounds, objective sampling, watchdogs and recovery without reducing the iterative functional sweep.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A single cap read or one user-chosen value cannot replace the repeated graph-based MSAC coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: MSAC, safe range, platform and full recovery contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Repeated cap changes and stress can throttle, destabilize or strand the server; OS install and AC removal are disruptive.

project_override_considerations: Project may select an approved tool/API instead of ILO UI, but must document equivalent license, cap enable/write/readback, history/sampling, iterative sweep and restoration coverage; unsupported ILO wording remains preserved.
expected_evidence: Approved target, license, OS/AC/workload baseline and original cap
Per-step write/readback with synchronized graph and power/thermal/performance series
Watchdog/abort audit and proof no unapproved step/retry occurred
Restored system/cap/workload health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Step 16 says stop at an MSAC value obtained previously, but no earlier step obtains or defines MSAC. ILO-specific licensing appears in a Common BMC case, and the procedure's multi-phase duration is not reconciled with 60-minute Machine Time.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Undefined terminal value and platform/control semantics make the iterative destructive workflow unbounded; these are core test-definition issues, not mere missing runtime inputs.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects PARTIAL execution because the proposed evidence omits nearly all functional phases and safety boundaries.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Confirms BLOCKED and its phase/safety requirements.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Overrides operator-gated PARTIAL because operator presence cannot invent MSAC or a safe stop.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Preserves this case's iterative sweep rather than merging it with simple get/set identities.

review_improvement: Makes the undefined end condition and cross-platform assumptions explicit before a repeated performance-limiting operation can run.
independent_technical_reasoning: An iterative search requires a defined lower bound, convergence/stop rule and anomaly response. Here MSAC is referenced but never measured, and the 5 W decrement could continue into unsafe or unsupported values. Together with disruptive OS/AC preparation, this makes the current workflow technically non-executable regardless of whether a package is available.
